title: Viktor Medvedchuk

fields.label: Position held
fields.value: People's Deputy of Ukraine, People's Deputy of Ukraine

summary: Viktor Volodymyrovych Medvedchuk is a former Ukrainian lawyer, business oligarch, and politician known for his pro-Kremlin stance and close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. He has been a significant figure in Ukrainian politics, particularly in relation to the country's geopolitical orientation and internal conflicts.

sections.heading: Early Life and Education
paragraphs: Viktor Medvedchuk was born on 7 August 1954 in Pochet, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russian SFSR. His father, Volodymyr Medvedchuk, faced imprisonment due to his involvement in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] nationalistic activities during World War II. The family returned to the [[ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic|Ukrainian SSR]] in the mid-1960s, settling in Kornyn, [[zhytomyr-oblast|Zhytomyr Oblast]]. Medvedchuk graduated from high school in Borova, [[fastiv|Fastiv]] Raion in 1971 and later enrolled at the Law School of KSU Shevchenko, where he graduated in 1978 as a lawyer.

sections.heading: Legal Career and Political Involvement
paragraphs: Medvedchuk began his legal career in 1979 and represented several dissidents, including poet Yuriy Lytvyn and [[vasyl-stus|Vasyl Stus]]. His defense strategies were criticized, particularly in the case of Stus, who ultimately died in a Soviet labor camp. In the early 1990s, he founded a successful legal firm and became a prominent political figure, joining the [[social-democratic-party-of-ukraine-united|Social Democratic Party of Ukraine]] in 1994.

Medvedchuk was first elected to the [[verkhovna-rada|Verkhovna Rada]] in 1997 and served multiple terms, including as First Deputy Chairman. He was head of the Presidential Administration under President [[leonid-kuchma|Leonid Kuchma]] from 2002 to 2005.

sections.heading: Recent Political Activities and Legal Troubles
paragraphs: In 2018, Medvedchuk became chairman of the pro-Russian political organization Ukrainian Choice and was elected as a People's Deputy of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] on 29 August 2019. He opposed Ukraine's integration into the European Union. Following accusations of financing terrorism and treason related to [[crimean-khanate|Crimea]], he faced legal challenges, including house arrest and eventual arrest by the [[security-service-of-ukraine|Security Service of Ukraine]] in April 2022.

On 21 September 2022, Medvedchuk was exchanged for Ukrainian prisoners of war and subsequently fled to Russia. On 13 January 2023, he was stripped of his position as a people's deputy by the Verkhovna Rada.

sections.heading: Controversies and Influence
paragraphs: Medvedchuk's political career has been marked by controversies, including allegations of involvement in suppressing the [[euromaidan|Euromaidan]] protests and connections to pro-[[kremlin|Kremlin]] activities. His close relationship with Russian President [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] has positioned him as a polarizing figure [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]'s political landscape, especially during times of heightened tensions between Ukraine and Russia.
